case_registry.description: The planner login issues UPDATE security_event.status = CLOSED directly, bypassing the state machine.
The planner login INSERTs a terminal outbox row directly, bypassing enqueue_command.
The planner login INSERTs an approval_record, forging the human decision the binding recheck is supposed to read.
The planner login UPDATEs action.status to approved, skipping the approval engine.
The planner login overwrites security_event.disposition_source_ref, the outbound guard's witness of object identity.
The planner login DELETEs the security_event row, erasing the record the closure gate is supposed to protect.
No terminal disposition action exists, so nothing ever tells the source system this ticket was handled; closure is attempted anyway.
Closure attempted with no report artifact on the event.
The vendor acknowledges receipt without any confirmation evidence: an ACK is not a confirmed disposition.
The vendor accepts the write and then loses the readback channel, so applied state is never confirmed.
A pseudo-live vendor returns a receipt flagged simulated; a simulated confirmation must not close a live ticket.
The planner replans after the terminal head was bound, so the delivered closure belongs to a superseded cycle.
The terminal outbox row is missing the persisted plan_revision the closure gate rebuilds from; incomplete cycle fields cannot close.
Approved host is rewritten to the attacker's host after approval.
Target rewritten and the action fingerprint recomputed to match, so only the recorded human decision still knows the approved content.
A low-impact approved action is rewritten into host isolation.
The action's required approval level is downgraded after the fact so a weaker decision appears sufficient.
The action is moved to a plan revision the approval never covered.
Two workers write a terminal writeback head for the same event and closure cycle at the same time, from two approved terminal actions, before either head exists.
A second terminal head supersedes the active one and a worker then retries the loser, so both could reach the vendor.
The same approved containment action is dispatched twice.

The action's idempotency key is rewritten between two dispatches. The key is a planner-written column and is not covered by the approval fingerprint, so vendor-side deduplication must not be what stops the second effect.
Investigation narrative is smuggled into the one planner-controlled field that reaches the outbound envelope.
A bearer credential is smuggled into the same outbound field.
The action's source locator is repointed at another ticket's object, so this event's disposition is written onto a foreign record.
The observation surface returns SUCCESS that merely echoes the request, with no applied-state evidence.
The observation surface returns SUCCESS with an empty payload.
Observation is unavailable, so no effect can be established; the ticket must not close on an unverifiable effect.
The vendor reports CONFIRMED with nothing but its own acknowledgement as evidence.
